transcript.text: bosch 24 not draining, water sitting in bottom. help

Standing water in a Bosch is usually a clog you can clear yourself in about 15 minutes. Work through these in order:

## 1. Check for an error code
If the display shows one:
• E24: Drain hose kinked/clogged or filter blocked
• E25: Drain pump blocked (often something stuck under the pump cover)

To reset or force a drain, press and hold Start (or Start/Reset) for about 3 seconds, close the door, and wait a couple of minutes.

## 2. Get the water out
Turn off power at the breaker or unplug the unit. Pull the bottom rack and scoop/sponge out the water (a turkey baster, cup, and towels work well).

## 3. Clean the filter (most common fix)
• In the back floor of the tub, twist the cylindrical filter counterclockwise and lift it out. The flat mesh screen comes out with it.
• Rinse under hot water and scrub with a soft brush to remove grease and food buildup.

## 4. Check the drain pump cover (fixes E25)
• With the filter out, look in the sump for a small plastic cover, often white or gray, with a tab.
• Pry the tab gently with a spoon handle and pull the cover up and toward you.
• Check underneath for broken glass, bone, seeds, labels, or twist ties jamming the impeller. Watch your fingers here because glass is common.
• The impeller should spin freely by hand (it'll feel slightly notchy, which is normal). Snap the cover back on firmly.

## 5. Check the drain path under the sink
• Drain hose: Look for kinks or crushing behind/under the unit. It should have a high loop (secured up under the countertop).
• Garbage disposal: If the disposal is new, the knockout plug inside the dishwasher inlet may never have been removed. Also run the disposal, since a full one can block drainage.
• Air gap (the small chrome cap by the faucet, if you have one): Pull the cap off and clear any gunk.
• Sink drain: If the kitchen sink is slow, the clog is in the house plumbing, not the dishwasher.

## 6. Test
Restore power, put the filter back (twist until it locks), and run a Rinse or short cycle. Listen during the drain:
• Pump hums but no water moves: There's still a blockage (pump cover area or hose).
• No sound at all from the pump: The drain pump has likely failed. It's a common part, around $40–$100, and a moderately easy DIY replacement, or a service call.

If you tell me the error code (if any), whether you hear the pump running, and whether this started after a new install or disposal, I can narrow it down further.
E:24 on display. humming at the end, slight bad smell. never cleaned the filter. where is it?

E:24 plus a never-cleaned filter almost certainly means the filter is clogged. The humming is the drain pump trying to push water through the blockage, and the smell is trapped food and grease.

## Where the filter is
1. Turn off power at the breaker or unplug the unit.
2. Pull out the bottom rack completely.
3. Look at the floor of the tub, toward the back (under where the lower spray arm sits). You'll see a round plastic handle, about 2-3 inches across, sitting in a recessed well. It's often under standing water, so bail some out first.
4. Twist the handle counterclockwise about a quarter turn and lift straight up. The cylindrical filter comes out, and the flat mesh screen around it lifts out too.

## Cleaning it
• Rinse both parts under hot water and scrub with a soft brush or old toothbrush. Since it's never been cleaned, expect sludge; a drop of dish soap helps cut grease.
• Wipe out the well the filter sat in. Food and debris collect there.

## While it's out (for the humming)
Look in the sump for the small drain pump cover (a plastic piece with a tab). Pop it up with a spoon handle and check for glass, seeds, bone, or labels jamming the impeller. Watch your fingers, since broken glass is common here. Snap it back firmly.

## Put it back
Seat the flat screen first, then insert the cylinder and twist clockwise until it locks. If it isn't locked, it can rattle or let debris through.

## Reset and test
Restore power, press and hold Start/Reset for ~3 seconds, close the door, and let it drain. Then run a Rinse or short cycle.

For the smell: Once it's draining, run an empty hot cycle with a cup of white vinegar upright on the top rack, or use a dishwasher cleaner.

Going forward: Clean the filter about once a month.

If E:24 comes back after this, check the drain hose under the sink for kinks and make sure the disposal is clear.
filter was clogged with food and a bit of broken glass. cleaned it, drains normally now, E:24 gone. should I do anything else?

Nice work. Since you found broken glass, a few quick follow-ups are worth doing:

## 1. Check for more glass (most important)
Glass shards often get past the filter and can jam or chip the drain pump impeller, causing E:25 or noisy draining later.
• With power off, remove the filter again and pop up the drain pump cover in the sump (plastic piece with a tab; pry gently with a spoon handle).
• Look for shards around the impeller. Use tongs, tweezers, or a damp paper towel, not bare fingers.
• Check that the impeller spins freely by hand, then snap the cover back firmly.
• Wipe the filter well and tub floor with a damp paper towel to pick up small slivers.

## 2. Check the spray arms
Food and glass bits can clog the spray holes and cause poor cleaning.
• Pull off the lower spray arm (it lifts or unclips) and the upper arm if easy.
• Shake out debris and clear any blocked holes with a toothpick. Rinse and reinstall.

## 3. Deal with the smell
Run an empty hot cycle with a cup of white vinegar upright on the top rack, or use a dishwasher cleaner tablet. Also wipe the door gasket and the bottom edge of the door, where gunk hides.

## 4. Going forward
• Clean the filter about once a month (more often if you don't pre-scrape dishes).
• Scrape large food scraps into the trash; no need to pre-rinse.
• Run the garbage disposal before starting the dishwasher if they share a drain.

If you later hear grinding or rattling during draining, or get E:25, that usually means more glass reached the pump.
